claim: copywin() can be used to copy a window completely onto another window
quote: man/curs_overlay.3x: copywin provides finer control over overlay/overwrite via source origin and destination rectangle; overlay=true is non-destructive. HOWTO: "The function copywin() can be used to copy a window completely onto another window" with rectangle and overlay flag.
earlier: From the HOWTO wording alone I would have matched; the man page confirms copywin can express a full-window copy.

claim: The values returned can be 1 (all is well), 0 (no such terminal), or -1 (some problem locating the terminfo database)
quote: man/curs_terminfo.3x: OK with errret 1 is normal; on ERR, errret 1 means hard-copy terminal, 0 means not found/generic, -1 means terminfo database not found. Intro prints the simplified 1/0/-1 "all is well" gloss.
earlier: Before the ERR/hard-copy case in the man page, the intro's three-value gloss looked correct.

claim: By calling setupterm() for each terminal, and saving and restoring cur_term, a program can use two or more terminals
quote: setupterm stores state in cur_term; set_curterm switches it (updates SP->_term, ospeed, PC, ttytype). Intro: save/restore cur_term for two or more terminals.
earlier: Before reading set_curterm, a raw pointer assign looked incomplete; set_curterm shows restoring the saved TERMINAL* is the supported switch.

claim: trace() sets the trace level; _tracef() is available only if you link with -lncurses_g
quote: man/curs_trace.3x: deprecated trace(); aside from curses_trace, other trace functions (including _tracef) are normally only in the debugging library e.g. libncurses_g.a. man/ncurses.3x documents -lncurses_g.
earlier: Same conclusion from curs_trace.3x alone; ncurses.3x only reinforced -lncurses_g.

claim: endwin() should called once
quote: Intro: "endwin() should called once at wrapup time for each terminal". man: must call endwin for each terminal; if newterm is used more than once for the same terminal, first opened is last endwin'd. Printed text lacks "be" and "once" alone omits per-terminal.
earlier: Before the man page, I might have treated it as a mere typo with correct "once" intent.

claim: It is only available only if
quote: Intro: "It is only available only if you link with -lncurses_g." man: "normally available only with the debugging library e.g., libncurses_g.a." Double "only" is erroneous wording.
earlier: Before comparing to the man page's single "only", the fragment looked like an incomplete but true availability note.

claim: Setupterm() also stores
quote: Intro continues: stores the names section in ttytype[]. man/term_variables.3x: setupterm copies the terminal name to ttytype. Fact matches; mid-sentence capital "Setupterm" is stylistic only.
earlier: The bare fragment looked incomplete until the intro/man ttytype sentences were opened.

claim: When ncurses returns that code, it calls resizeterm
quote: man/resizeterm.3x: SIGWINCH handler path calls resizeterm, which ungetch's KEY_RESIZE for the next wgetch. Order is resizeterm then KEY_RESIZE return, not call-on-return as the intro states.
earlier: The intro's wording alone would have matched; the man page reverses the causal order.

claim: The refresh will pick up the new screen size from the xterm's environment
quote: Size comes from the OS (e.g. TIOCGWINSZ); LINES/COLUMNS override if set. Intro claims refresh picks size "from the xterm's environment," which is not how a live xterm resize updates an already-running process.
earlier: Before lib_setup.c, the man page's env-override note made the intro sound merely incomplete rather than wrong.

claim: Note that you will also have to call def_shell_mode and def_prog_mode on each tty yourself
quote: newterm → _nc_setupscreen already calls def_shell_mode and def_prog_mode; man: done automatically by initscr, with one save area per newterm screen. Manual per-tty calls are not required.
earlier: From the intro alone the claim seemed plausible; setupscreen shows it is automatic.

claim: Ncurses supports up 16 colors, unlike SVr4 curses which defines only 8. While most terminals which provide color allow only 8 colors, about a quarter (including XFree86 xterm) support 16 colors.
quote: Intro says "supports up 16 colors" (missing "to") and treats 16 as the story. man/NEWS discuss terminals with COLORS greater than 16 and 256-color practice; 16 is no longer the ceiling.
earlier: Before NEWS/COLORS>16 notes, the 16-vs-8 special-feature claim looked still current aside from the missing "to".

claim: the attribute of erased blanks is normal unless and until it is modified by the functions bkgdset() or wbkgdset()
quote: man: erase fills with the background character set via bkgdset/wbkgdset; blank cells combine with that background. Intro's newer-versions background-erase note matches current behavior.
earlier: Same match from the intro and curs_bkgd.3x; no later source changed it.

claim: every macro entry point have a corresponding function which may be linked
quote: Intro: XSI requirement that every macro entry point have a corresponding function if the macro is #undef'd. man/ncurses.3x notes macros exclusive of function definitions as a NOTES caveat in general, without retracting the XSI correspondence goal for ncurses.
earlier: Without the intro's XSI sentence, the man NOTES about macro-only symbols would have pushed toward disagrees.

claim: mvprintw(24, 0, "Press F1 to Exit")
quote: JustForFun/hanoi.c is only referenced by path in the HOWTO, not shipped under primary evidence trees. curs_move: (y,x) outside window boundaries yields ERR; on a 24-line stdscr valid rows are 0..23, so y=24 is out of range.
earlier: Before applying window-bound rules, missing JustForFun sources would have been can't tell.

claim: mvprintw(24, 0, ...) for "Press F1 to Exit" and "You Win !!!"
quote: JustForFun/shuffle.c not present under primary evidence paths. Same bound rule: row 24 is outside a 24-line window.
earlier: Would have been can't tell from the HOWTO path reference alone.

claim: #define STATUSY 25
quote: JustForFun/tt.c not under primary evidence paths. LINES is the screen height; a fixed STATUSY 25 is outside 0..LINES-1 for common 24-line screens.
earlier: Without the move/LINES constraints, missing tt.c would force can't tell.

claim: #define KEY_F1 265
quote: KEY_F(0) is 0410 octal (264); KEY_F(n) is KEY_F0+(n), so KEY_F(1)=265. The numeric value matches.
earlier: Same after Caps alone; MKkey_defs only confirmed the KEY_F0+(n) formula.

claim: http://www2.linuxjournal.com/lj-issues/issue5/2807.html
quote: HOWTO still prints that Linux Journal URL. Whether the URL resolves is outside the repository.
earlier: Opening only the HOWTO citation cannot settle link liveness; an HTTP fetch outside primary evidence would be required.

claim: Curses::Form, from the CPAN All Modules page
quote: HOWTO names Curses::Form / Curses::Widgets. Existence on CPAN is outside-repo.
earlier: Same: the HOWTO mention alone cannot verify the CPAN module.

claim: Thomas E. Dickey has maintained ncurses since 1.9.9e
quote: AUTHORS: principal contributors since 1.9.9e, TD first. NEWS: changes since 1.9.9e recorded by Thomas E Dickey. ANNOUNCE: ongoing development / maintainer role for Dickey.
earlier: AUTHORS alone already matched; NEWS/ANNOUNCE only corroborated.

claim: Thomas E. Dickey wrote or revised most of the manual pages
quote: Widespread Thomas E. Dickey copyright lines on current man pages; ANNOUNCE credits ongoing development to Dickey. Supports wrote/revised most pages.
earlier: Sampling a few man headers was enough; ANNOUNCE did not change the verdict.

claim: Thomas E. Dickey, maintainer since ncurses 1.9.9e
quote: Same maintainer-since-1.9.9e evidence as L194.
earlier: Identical to L194 after AUTHORS.

claim: The third objective (standards conformance)
quote: Ordered objectives: (1) source-compatible, (2) XSI/standards conformance, (3) high-quality, (4) featureful. Later prose wrongly calls standards conformance the third objective.
earlier: Reading only the "third objective" sentence would have matched the claim as printed.

claim: This is a majordomo list
quote: hackguide calls bug-ncurses a majordomo list. ANNOUNCE still shows request-address subscribe syntax but never names majordomo; actual list software is not established in-repo.
earlier: From hackguide alone I would have matched; ANNOUNCE removes certainty without confirming the MTA.

claim: `trace()`
quote: hackguide tells bug reporters to insert trace(). man still documents deprecated trace(); debugging builds still provide it.
earlier: Deprecated status in curs_trace.3x does not remove the symbol the hackguide names.

claim: Test frames for the library algorithms are in the progs directory
quote: hackguide: tiny test frames (e.g. mvcur, hashmap) in progs. progs/ holds tic/tput/tset/infocmp/clear/tabs/toe utilities only—no such test frames.
earlier: Before listing progs/, the hackguide assertion looked plausible.

claim: If the entire sequence takes less than 1 second
quote: Default ESCDELAY is 1000 ms (1 second). Timed wait after a possible function-key prefix matches the hackguide's "less than 1 second" rule at default settings.
earlier: Same after seeing ESCDELAY=1000; the man page only named the variable.

claim: `timed_wait()`
quote: hackguide names timed_wait(). Source exports _nc_timed_wait only; no timed_wait symbol.
earlier: Before searching the tree, the hackguide name looked like the real function.

claim: `lib_doupdate.c`
quote: No lib_doupdate.c file remains. tty_update.c header still says "lib_doupdate.c" as the historical name of doupdate's home.
earlier: A filename search alone looked like missing; the tty_update.c banner shows the rename.

claim: `_nc_mvcur_scrolln()` in `lib_mvcur.c`
quote: No _nc_mvcur_scrolln exists. hardscroll calls _nc_scrolln; lib_mvcur.c may call _nc_scrolln. Claimed symbol/location are absent.
earlier: Before the symbol search, the hackguide identifier looked real.
